lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: Who carries the risk? Fully insured: The **insurer**. The employer pays a fixed premium; if claims are high, the insurer loses. Self-funded (ASO): The **employer**. Claims are paid from the employer's own money.
lines.say: Who carries the risk? Fully insured: The insurer. The employer pays a fixed premium; if claims are high, the insurer loses. Self-funded (A S O): The employer. Claims are paid from the employer's own money.

lines.raw: What does the insurer do? Fully insured: Everything: pays claims and takes the risk. Self-funded (ASO): Only **administration**: network, claims processing, ID cards. **ASO** = Administrative Services Only.
lines.say: What does the insurer do? Fully insured: Everything: pays claims and takes the risk. Self-funded (A S O): Only administration: network, claims processing, I D cards. A S O = Administrative Services Only.

lines.raw: Who uses it? Fully insured: Many small and mid-size employers. Self-funded (ASO): Most large employers.
lines.say: Who uses it? Fully insured: Many small and mid-size employers. Self-funded (A S O): Most large employers.

lines.raw: Main rules. Fully insured: State insurance laws and federal rules. Self-funded (ASO): Mainly federal law (ERISA); many state insurance rules do not apply.
lines.say: Main rules. Fully insured: State insurance laws and federal rules. Self-funded (A S O): Mainly federal law (E R I S A); many state insurance rules do not apply.

scenes.section: Product types: how the network works

lines.raw: Common US product types.
lines.say: Common U S product types.

lines.raw: **HMO**. Full name: Health Maintenance Organization. Out-of-network covered?: No (except emergencies). Referral to see a specialist?: Usually yes, from your primary care doctor (PCP). In short: Cheapest, most rules.
lines.say: H M O. Full name: Health Maintenance Organization. Out-of-network covered?: No (except emergencies). Referral to see a specialist?: Usually yes, from your primary care doctor (P C P). In short: Cheapest, most rules.

lines.raw: **PPO**. Full name: Preferred Provider Organization. Out-of-network covered?: Yes, but you pay more. Referral to see a specialist?: No. In short: Most freedom, higher premium.
lines.say: P P O. Full name: Preferred Provider Organization. Out-of-network covered?: Yes, but you pay more. Referral to see a specialist?: No. In short: Most freedom, higher premium.

lines.raw: **EPO**. Full name: Exclusive Provider Organization. Out-of-network covered?: No (except emergencies). Referral to see a specialist?: Usually no. In short: Network only, but no referrals.
lines.say: E P O. Full name: Exclusive Provider Organization. Out-of-network covered?: No (except emergencies). Referral to see a specialist?: Usually no. In short: Network only, but no referrals.

lines.raw: **POS**. Full name: Point of Service. Out-of-network covered?: Yes, but you pay more. Referral to see a specialist?: Usually yes. In short: A mix of HMO and PPO.
lines.say: P O S. Full name: Point of Service. Out-of-network covered?: Yes, but you pay more. Referral to see a specialist?: Usually yes. In short: A mix of H M O and P P O.

lines.raw: **HDHP**. Full name: High Deductible Health Plan. Out-of-network covered?: Depends on the network type underneath. Referral to see a specialist?: Depends. In short: Low premium, high deductible; can pair with an **HSA**.
lines.say: H D H P. Full name: High Deductible Health Plan. Out-of-network covered?: Depends on the network type underneath. Referral to see a specialist?: Depends. In short: Low premium, high deductible; can pair with an H S A.
